newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slips as state-run bank buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slips as state-run bank buys dollars.

text.p: The rupee slipped to 35.85/86 on Thursday from its 35.80/81 opening on large dollar buying by a state-run bank, dealers said.
The bank, based in western India, was buying dollars for a state-run firm, a dealer at a foreign bank said.
Some dealers said State Bank of India was in the market.
"The rupee should see a welcome two-way movement from 35.75 to 35.85 now," said a dealer. The rupee has moved in a narrow groove of 35.76/80 over the past week.
Spot dollar was quoted at 35.85/87 in latest deals.
